newsitem.title: GERMANY: SAP blots model record with insider probe.
newsitem.headline: SAP blots model record with insider probe.

text.p: Software maker SAP AG , whose dizzying ascent on the German stock market has made it one of the most popular stocks, emerged Monday as the focus of an insider trading probe.

Armed with a list of names of suspected offenders, Frankfurt prosecutors said they were investigating allegations that a large group of SAP staff members and associates dealt illegally in its shares in a phase of extreme price volatility last year.

The probe concerned more than 100 individuals in its early stages, a spokesman for Germany's stock market watchdog told Reuters, and could become the most serious case since insider trading was criminalized here in 1994.

Investors showed their disapproval by sending SAP's DAX-listed preferred shares plummeting as much as 5 percent in early trading Monday, but the stock regained ground in a booming market session and closed up 3.10 marks ($1.80) at 324.50 ($188), a rise which still lagged clearly behind the broader market.
SAP's stock market record has been meteoric -- it has tripled in value since early 1995, when news that it was to join the DAX fanned a flurry of buy interest.

The biggest blip, and the focus of the insider probe, came after news last October of an unexpected slowdown in third-quarter growth. That news slashed SAP's stock by a quarter, although they have risen to new record highs since.

The Federal Securities Trading Supervisory Authority, the linchpin of Germany's crackdown on insider deals, began an investigation into the price drop and found enough evidence to pass on the case to prosecutors.

"The investigation is looking at the use of insider information in the trading of shares," prosecution spokesman Job Tilmann said. "This is probably the most serious case we have seen here," said supervisory authority spokesman Juergen Oberfrank.

The authority said over 100 "primary and secondary insiders" were named in the initial probe -- the first category implies staff at SAP and banks and the second their relatives or friends -- making it one of the largest it has ever handled. "But we expect that this number will fall as time goes by," Oberfrank added.
